42862277.text: Among prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-directed radioligand therapies (RLT), ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 is supported by two peer-reviewed phase III randomised controlled trials in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (VISION and PSMAfore) and one in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (PSMAddition). This structured narrative review uses eight predefined PubMed evidence sets, yielding 931 unique records after deduplication, to describe the study-design distribution and evidence-maturity profile of established and emerging PSMA-RLT strategies, including ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617, other Lu-177 PSMA agents, ²²⁵Ac, ¹⁶¹Tb, ²¹²Pb, ²¹¹At, and ⁹⁰Y. The review addresses five evidence questions: the differential patient-selection criteria between TheraP and VISION; rPFS-to-OS interpretation in PSMAfore; the sequencing implications of earlier hormone-sensitive RLT use; xerostomia and daughter-nuclide redistribution as unresolved development barriers for ²²⁵Ac-PSMA; and whether the microdosimetric rationale for ¹⁶¹Tb-PSMA is supported by clinical comparative data. The current evidence base identifies ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 as the most mature PSMA-RLT platform, while emerging radionuclides remain dependent on prospective clinical differentiation.

42914177.text: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has clinical activity in human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-low and -ultralow tumors in addition to HER2-positive tumors. However, no consistent correlation has been observed between traditional HER2 scoring criteria and response to T-DXd in HER2-low and HER2-ultralow tumors. There is a need for complementary approaches to monitor T-DXd delivery in vivo and potentially improve understanding of which tumors may benefit from T-DXd therapy. This study evaluated tumor uptake of radiolabeled T-DXd in tumors with varying HER2 protein levels using PET in treatment-naïve tumors and during T-DXd therapy. Methods: Chelator-conjugated T-DXd or trastuzumab was prepared via conventional lysine conjugation and radiolabeled with 64Cu. The binding and in vitro cytotoxicity of the conjugates were determined in cancer cell lines. PET/CT was performed across 11 tumor models (representing 5 tumor types), including cell xenografts, patient-derived xenografts, and syngeneic models in both subcutaneous and orthotopic models. Image-based tumor uptake of the radiolabeled antibodies was quantified in all models. In the treatment studies, mice bearing CT26-hHER2 tumors that express heterogeneous HER2 with an immunohistochemistry score of 2+ levels received weekly coinjections of therapeutic T-DXd (6 mg/kg) together with imaging-dose [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd (4 mg/kg), corresponding to a total T-DXd administered dose of 10 mg/kg. Results: [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd was obtained at a radiochemical purity of at least 98%. Purified [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd bound to cells in a concentration-dependent manner and had a positive correlation between HER2 protein levels and bound T-DXd. Conjugation of T-DXd to NOTA did not affect T-DXd binding or cytotoxicity in cancer cells. [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd mean tumor uptake varied across models (7.45 ± 1.28 to 19.10 ± 2.50 %ID/mL), and the mean uptake was similar to that of the parental antibody 64Cu-labeled trastuzumab. Preimaging doses of either trastuzumab or pertuzumab did not affect [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd uptake in tumors. There was a positive correlation between the change in [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd uptake and the change in tumor volume between weeks 1 and 2 of T-DXd treatment (P < 0.01) in CT26.hHER2 tumors grown in immunocompetent mice. Conclusion: [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd PET detects antibody-drug accumulation in tumors with low HER2 protein levels and may provide an early imaging biomarker associated with response. These studies show the potential of using HER2-targeted imaging in preclinical models to noninvasively assess antibody-drug conjugate delivery and explore imaging-based biomarkers associated with T-DXd response.

42969977.text: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects up to 38% of the population globally. Liver biopsy, the historical reference standard, is invasive, subject to sampling error and not scalable. MRI-based biomarkers provide non-invasive, quantitative whole liver assessment. MRI proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) is the most accurate noninvasive measure of steatosis (thresholds of 6.4%, 17.4% and 22.1% for grades ≥1, ≥2 and 3), and a ≥30% relative reduction is associated with histologic response. Liver stiffness by magnetic resonance elastography (MRE-LS) is the most accurate imaging biomarker for fibrosis: MRE-LS of 3.1-4.4 kPa corresponds to F2-F3 and ≥5 kPa to cirrhosis, and each 1-kPa increase is associated with a 43% higher risk of hepatic decompensation. Iron-corrected T1 is a sensitive but nonspecific marker of disease activity whose prognostic value requires further study. Composite scores, MAST, MEFIB, and MASH Resolution Index, combine imaging and blood tests for advanced fibrosis diagnosis and response assessment. MRE is cost-effective compared with vibration-controlled transient elastography for detecting advanced fibrosis. Artificial intelligence may broaden access by automating analysis and enabling PDFF from routine MRI. We review the evidence supporting these biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis and regulatory use, and their role in clinical trials and in treatment decisions for approved MASH therapies.

43019227.text: Isolated bilateral renal metastasis from esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is extremely rare. We report a 63-year-old man with ESCC treated with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy and esophagectomy followed by anti-PD-1 maintenance, in whom follow-up 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated multiple bilateral renal lesions with intense 18F-FDG uptake. CT-guided biopsy confirmed metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. This case highlights that new isolated renal lesions during cancer immunotherapy should not be assumed to be immune-related nephritis and underscores the value of 18F-FDG PET/CT and biopsy in establishing the diagnosis.

43023627.label: Background
43023627.text: Hepatic proton density fat fraction (PDFF) is often reported as a whole-liver mean, without a population reference for individual fat distribution.

43023627.label: Purpose
43023627.text: To construct longitudinal, sex-specific three-dimensional PDFF atlases and assess regional fat loss, sex differences in heterogeneity, and metabolic associations.

43023627.label: Study type
43023627.text: Prospective; secondary analysis of a randomized lifestyle intervention trial.

43023627.label: Population
43023627.text: A total of 127 adults with obesity imaged at baseline ( V 1 , 73 female [F], 54 male [M]), after an 8-week low-caloric diet ( V 2 , 49F/32M), and after 12-month weight maintenance ( V 3 , 40F/32M).

43023627.label: Assessment
43023627.text: Sex- and visit-specific atlases were built by deformable registration; z-maps quantified voxel-wise deviation from the matched atlas. Six heterogeneity features (standard deviation [σx], coefficient of variation [CV], entropy [ H ]; z- skewness, z-kurtosis, volume fraction z > 2) were compared between sexes and correlated, cross-sectionally and longitudinally, with hepatocellular, glycemic, adiposity markers and triglycerides, and longitudinally with steatosis remission (PDFF < 5%).

43023627.label: Statistical tests
43023627.text: Welch t-test; Spearman correlation (ρ); Benjamini-Hochberg correction within each test set. Significance at adjusted p < 0.05.

43023627.label: Results
43023627.text: Liver PDFF decreased significantly from V 1 to V 2 in males (13.6% ± 7.0% to 6.6% ± 2.5%) and females (9.1% ± 6.2% to 5.9% ± 3.3%) with regionally non-uniform, sex-specific patterns. At V 1 , σx and H were significantly higher in males and CV, z-skewness and z-kurtosis in females; at V 2 , σx (males) and z-skewness and z-kurtosis (females) remained significant; no feature differed at V 3 (adjusted p = [0.583-0.953]). Cross-sectionally, features correlated with hepatocellular, glycemic and adiposity markers, more extensively in females. Longitudinally, significant correlations were almost limited to adiposity (V1 to V3: CV × visceral fat volume in females, ρ = -0.65; CV × visceral PDFF in males, ρ = -0.67); apart from H × gamma-glutamyl transferase in females, no feature tracked hepatocellular, glycemic or steatosis remission outcomes (adjusted p = [0.051-0.999], [0.092-0.999], and [0.073-0.887]).

43023627.label: Data conclusion
43023627.text: Hepatic fat loss showed spatially heterogeneous and sex-specific patterns. Heterogeneity reflected metabolic state cross-sectionally but mainly adiposity change longitudinally.

43051027.label: Purpose
43051027.text: To determine the diagnostic performance and interobserver agreement of MRI for differentiating mucinous from non-mucinous pancreatic cystic lesions (PCLs) and identifying advanced neoplasia using surgical pathology as the reference standard.

43051027.label: Methods
43051027.text: This retrospective single-center study included surgically resected PCLs with preoperative MRI (2019-2025). Three independent readers blindly assessed cyst subtype and imaging features, including worrisome features (WF) and high-risk stigmata (HRS) according to the 2024 Kyoto guideline. Consensus interpretation was established with a fourth senior abdominal radiologist. Diagnostic performance for mucinous lesion characterization and advanced neoplasia (high-grade dysplasia and invasive carcinoma) was evaluated. Interobserver agreement was assessed using Fleiss κ and Gwet AC1. Logistic regression and ROC analyses identified imaging predictors of advanced neoplasia.

43051027.label: Results
43051027.text: A total of 85 patients were included (mean age, 66.8 ± 12.5 years; 50.6 % female). At pathology, 70/85 lesions (82.4 %) were mucinous and 23/85 (27.1 %) represented advanced neoplasia, including 21 high-grade dysplasia and two IPMN-derived PDAC. MRI consensus interpretation achieved 100 % sensitivity, 80 % specificity, and 96.5 % accuracy for identifying mucinous lesions. MRI demonstrated 52.2 % sensitivity and 67.7 % specificity for advanced neoplasia using WF or HRS, whereas HRS alone improved specificity (95.2 %) at the expense of sensitivity (21.7 %). All readers correctly identified both cases of IPMN-derived PDAC. Interobserver agreement for cyst subtype classification was fair by Fleiss κ but substantial by Gwet AC1, whereas agreement for detecting advanced neoplasia was moderate. Main pancreatic duct diameter independently predicted advanced neoplasia (OR, 1.18; 95 % CI, 1.01-1.38; p = 0.042) and outperformed cyst size (AUC, 0.69 vs 0.56).

43051027.label: Conclusion
43051027.text: In this surgically selected cohort, consensus MRI differentiates mucinous from nonmucinous PCLs with high sensitivity. Detection of advanced neoplasia, particularly noninvasive high-grade dysplasia, remains challenging because of overlap with low-grade lesions. Fair-to-moderate interobserver agreement highlights the challenges of MRI-based risk stratification. The surgically selected cohort provides histopathologic confirmation but should be considered when interpreting performance estimates in the broader surveillance population.

43076677.text: A 76-year-old woman presented with a 6-month history of progressive anorexia, unintentional weight loss, and heartburn. She reported no abdominal pain, vomiting, gastrointestinal bleeding, or fever but reported intermittent bilateral lower-extremity edema. Physical examination revealed a relatively firm abdominal wall with a palpable upper abdominal mass and no peritoneal signs. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated normocytic anemia (hemoglobin level, 91 g/L; reference range, 115-150 g/L), mild thrombocytosis, no leukocytosis (white blood cell count, 6.24 × 109/L; reference range, 3.5 × 109/L to 9.5 × 109/L), severe hypoalbuminemia (albumin level, 19.5 g/L; reference range, 40.0-55.0 g/L) with low total protein, and electrolyte abnormalities including hyponatremia (sodium level, 128.4 mmol/L; reference range, 137-147 mmol/L) and hypocalcemia (total calcium level, 1.80-1.92 mmol/L; reference range, 2.11-2.52 mmol/L). The D-dimer level was markedly elevated (4900 µg/L [26.8 nmol/L]; reference range, <500 μg/L [<2.7 nmol/L]), whereas serum creatinine level was within the reference range, and serum tumor markers (α-fetoprotein, carcinoembryonic antigen, and carbohydrate antigen 19-9) were not elevated. Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis and fluorine 18 (18F) fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT were performed.

43076977.label: Purpose
43076977.text: B7-H3 is a promising theranostic target in lung cancer and other solid tumors, while B7-H3-targeted radiopharmaceuticals still warrant further optimization. We developed 177Lu-DOTA-hJ42 using a self-developed humanized anti-B7-H3 monoclonal antibody and compared it with 177Lu-DOTA-huM30, based on a recombinantly expressed antibody with the disclosed sequence of ifinatamab, the antibody component of DS-7300a.

43076977.label: Methods
43076977.text: The anti-B7-H3 monoclonal antibodies hJ42 and huM30 were conjugated with DOTA and radiolabeled with 177Lu for head-to-head evaluation. Radiochemical properties, binding affinity, cellular uptake, and internalization were assessed in vitro. Single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT) imaging, biodistribution, therapeutic efficacy, safety, and dosimetry were subsequently evaluated in B7-H3-positive lung cancer patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models.

43076977.label: Results
43076977.text: Both radioimmunoconjugates showed favorable in vitro stability, with IC50 values of 2.184 nM for 177Lu-DOTA-hJ42 and 2.499 nM for 177Lu-DOTA-huM30. Both exhibited time-dependent, B7-H3-specific cellular uptake and efficient internalization. Biodistribution studies in lung cancer PDX models revealed sustained tumor uptake (> 40%ID/g) and favorable tumor/normal tissue ratios, with maximum ratio of approximately 60. SPECT/CT imaging further demonstrated persistent tumor retention in PDX models, whereas background evaluation in non-tumor-bearing B-hB7-H3 humanized mice showed relatively low uptake in normal organs. Single administrations of either 177Lu-DOTA-hJ42 or 177Lu-DOTA-huM30 at 7.4 or 14.8 MBq significantly suppressed tumor growth, with no obvious treatment-related toxicity observed during the study period.

43076977.label: Conclusion
43076977.text: Collectively, 177Lu-DOTA-hJ42 enabled specific imaging and effective treatment of B7-H3-positive lung cancer and performed comparably to 177Lu-DOTA-huM30, supporting hJ42 as a promising antibody scaffold for developing B7-H3-targeted radionuclide conjugates.
